input: Organize all my digital photos by year

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Photos may be scattered across multiple devices, drives, or cloud services — knowing exactly what is included determines the complexity and starting point of the task.
The operating system, storage location (local vs. cloud), and existing folder structure determine which tools and methods are practical.
The total number of photos and available storage space affects whether a manual, semi-automated, or fully automated approach is needed.
The year assigned to each photo could come from the file name, EXIF metadata, or date modified — this choice directly affects accuracy and the tools required.
The user may want only top-level year folders, or sub-folders by month or event within each year — this shapes the entire folder structure.
If duplicates exist across devices or accounts, the user needs to decide whether to deduplicate as part of this task, which significantly changes the scope.
Knowing whether the original file locations should be preserved, moved, or copied determines whether this is a destructive reorganization or a safe, reversible one.

gold.taskTitle: Organize all digital photos by year
gold.taskDescription: Sort and restructure the user's entire digital photo collection into a year-based organizational system.

questions.title: Where are your photos currently stored?
questions.description: Identify all source locations — e.g., a single PC folder, multiple external drives, iCloud, Google Photos, phone storage — to determine what needs to be consolidated.

questions.title: What device and operating system will you use?
questions.description: Establish the working environment (Windows, Mac, Linux, mobile) and whether photos live locally or in the cloud, which determines which tools and scripts are available.

questions.title: Roughly how many photos are you dealing with?
questions.description: Get an order-of-magnitude estimate (hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands) to decide whether a manual, bulk-rename tool, or custom script approach is most practical.

questions.title: What date source should determine each photo's year?
questions.description: Clarify whether to use EXIF capture date, file creation date, file modification date, or file name — this directly affects sorting accuracy, especially for scanned or downloaded photos.

questions.title: Should year folders contain sub-folders like months or events?
questions.description: Determine the desired depth of the folder hierarchy — year-only, year/month, or year/event — which defines the entire target structure before any files are moved.

questions.title: Do you want duplicates removed as part of this process?
questions.description: Find out if deduplication is in scope, since many collections have duplicate files across devices or backups, which would meaningfully expand the task.

questions.title: Should files be moved or copied to the new structure?
questions.description: Establish whether the original file locations must be preserved as a safety backup (copy) or whether files should be relocated permanently (move), determining risk and storage requirements.
